title: Desktop cloud-task bootstrap state-dir contract between backend launcher and wait script
answers: How does the desktop cloud task bootstrap run in the background?
pnpm bootstrap:cloud-task:wait exits 2 or 124, what does it mean?
Changing the desktop bootstrap state directory or timeout
body:
The backend launcher and the agent-side wait script share a file protocol and must change together.
- Backend: `_prepare_posthog_desktop_cloud_task` and constants `DESKTOP_BOOTSTRAP_STATE_DIR`, `DESKTOP_BOOTSTRAP_WAIT_SCRIPT`, `DESKTOP_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` in products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/activities/provision_sandbox.py.
- Agent side: products/desktop/scripts/wait-cloud-task-bootstrap.sh, wired as `bootstrap:cloud-task:wait` in products/desktop/package.json.
- Files in the state dir: `started` (epoch), `log`, `build.pid`, `launcher.pid`, `exit` (written via exit.tmp then mv so it is never partial). The wait script reads `started`, `exit`, `log`.
- Exit codes: 2 = nothing launched; 124 = build timed out; otherwise the build's own code.
- The wait script's default timeout (960s) must stay longer than the backend timeout (900s) plus the `timeout -k 30` grace.
- Docs to update too: products/desktop/AGENTS.md and docs/internal/cloud-task-sandbox.md.
applies: Desktop bootstrap in posthog/posthog dev-stack cloud task sandboxes
